When a login challenge is issued, the hardware key cryptographically signs the response using the registered site's exact origin (domain). If the user is on a phishing site with a different domain, the key's signature will not match the expected origin and authentication fails automatically — the key literally cannot be fooled by a fake site. SMS codes can be intercepted via SIM swapping or relayed in real time by a phishing proxy. Email OTP is vulnerable if the email account is compromised. TOTP app codes can be captured and forwarded by a real-time phishing proxy within the 30-second validity window. Push notifications are susceptible to MFA fatigue attacks. For highest assurance, FIDO2 hardware keys are the gold standard.

prompt: A retail store installs visible security cameras at all entrances with posted notices. What dual security function do these cameras serve?

options.text: They are purely decorative with no real security function
They act as a deterrent control (discouraging criminal behavior) and a detective control (capturing evidence of incidents)
They only function as a detective control after an incident occurs
They provide access control by physically preventing unauthorized entry

explanation: Visible security cameras serve two distinct security functions. As a deterrent control, their presence discourages potential criminals from attempting theft, vandalism, or unauthorized access because they know they may be identified. Studies show that visible cameras measurably reduce crime in surveilled areas. As a detective control, recorded footage provides evidence for law enforcement, helps identify perpetrators, reconstructs timelines of events, and supports insurance claims and legal proceedings. Legal considerations include posting visible notices (required in many jurisdictions), prohibiting cameras in private areas such as restrooms, complying with audio-recording laws, and establishing a footage retention policy (typically 30 to 90 days). Cameras do not physically prevent entry and therefore are not access controls.

prompt: A company wants shared public kiosk workstations where anyone can use them without a password, and all changes are discarded after each session. Which Windows feature best supports this requirement?

options.text: Create a shared standard user account with a known password
Configure Windows Kiosk Mode (Assigned Access) or use a third-party reset tool like Deep Freeze to restore the system after each session
Give all users administrator accounts for convenience
Disable all user accounts and configure the PC to boot directly to the desktop

explanation: For secure public kiosk workstations, Windows Kiosk Mode (Assigned Access) restricts the session to a single designated app (such as a browser) and provides no access to the rest of the system. All settings and data from a kiosk session are discarded when the session ends. Alternatively, third-party tools such as Faronics Deep Freeze freeze the system state and automatically restore it to a clean configuration on every reboot, discarding all user changes. The built-in Guest account (disabled by default) allows password-free login with restricted access but does not provide automatic session cleanup. Simply sharing a password on a standard or admin account creates security and accountability problems. Kiosk Mode is managed via Settings → Accounts → Other users → Set up a kiosk, and works well for single-purpose deployments.

prompt: Documents are stuck in a Windows print queue and cannot be deleted, even after canceling all jobs. What is the correct procedure to clear the stuck queue?

options.text: Reinstall the printer driver
Stop the Print Spooler service, delete all files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\, then restart the service
Restart the computer and wait 10 minutes for the queue to clear
Uninstall the printer and re-add it

explanation: The correct stuck queue resolution: 1) Stop the Print Spooler service: open Services (services.msc), find Print Spooler, click Stop. Alternatively: net stop spooler in an elevated Command Prompt. 2) Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\ and delete all files inside the folder, but do NOT delete the folder itself. 3) Restart the Print Spooler: net start spooler. The queue will now be empty. The quick command-line version: net stop spooler && del /Q /F /S C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\* && net start spooler. Print jobs get stuck due to corrupt spool files, a crashed driver, or a printer that went offline mid-job. If the Print Spooler crashes repeatedly after clearing, the printer driver itself is likely corrupted and should be removed and reinstalled.

prompt: A user's display goes black for a few seconds then recovers with a notification: 'Display driver stopped responding and has recovered.' This repeats regularly. What is the most likely cause and first fix?

options.text: The monitor needs to be replaced
TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) fired because of an unstable or outdated GPU driver — update or roll back the GPU driver
A bad RAM stick is causing the display issue — run MemTest86
The CPU is overheating — clean the heatsink and reapply thermal paste

explanation: Windows TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) monitors the GPU and resets it if the graphics driver stops responding for more than 2 seconds. The display goes black briefly while the driver restarts. Common causes: an outdated driver, a driver version incompatible with recent Windows updates, GPU overheating (check temperatures with GPU-Z or MSI Afterburner), an underpowered PSU that cannot supply peak GPU power, or an overclocked GPU running at unstable settings. Troubleshooting steps: 1) Check Event Viewer → System for Event ID 4101. 2) Download the latest driver directly from the GPU manufacturer (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) rather than relying on Windows Update. 3) If the issue started after a driver update, use Device Manager → Display Adapters → Roll Back Driver. 4) Monitor GPU temperatures under load.

prompt: A Windows 11 PC displays 'Windows is not activated' after a motherboard replacement. What is the most likely cause and the correct resolution?

options.text: Windows is corrupted — reinstall from scratch
The hardware change triggered re-activation — use the activation troubleshooter or link a Microsoft account to reactivate the digital license
The hard drive is failing — run chkdsk
The product key was used on too many devices — purchase a new license

explanation: Windows activation ties the license to a hardware fingerprint. A motherboard replacement is the most significant hardware change and commonly triggers deactivation. Retail licenses are transferable to new hardware; OEM licenses are tied to the original motherboard and technically cannot be transferred. For a digital license linked to a Microsoft account: Settings → System → Activation → Troubleshoot → I changed hardware on this device recently → sign in with the associated Microsoft account to reactivate. If activation fails or no Microsoft account is linked, contact Microsoft Support via the telephone activation option (automated system). Command-line tools: slmgr.vbs /dli shows license type and status; slmgr.vbs /ato attempts online activation. Until activated, Windows is fully functional but displays a watermark and limits personalization settings.

prompt: After installing a new peer-to-peer application, it cannot connect to remote peers while all other internet apps work fine. What is the first thing to check?

options.text: The ISP is blocking peer-to-peer traffic on the account
Windows Defender Firewall may have blocked the app when Windows prompted for access — add a manual exception in Firewall settings
The application is malware — uninstall it immediately
The router needs to be replaced

explanation: When a new application first attempts to use the network, Windows Firewall shows a prompt asking the user to allow or block it. If the user clicked Block or dismissed the prompt, the app is permanently blocked. To fix this: Control Panel → Windows Defender Firewall → Allow an app or feature through Windows Defender Firewall → Change settings → find the application in the list and check the appropriate network checkboxes (Private and/or Public). If the app is not listed, click Allow another app, browse to the executable, and add it. Alternatively, create an inbound rule in wf.msc. As a quick diagnostic, temporarily disable Windows Firewall to confirm it is the cause, then immediately re-enable it and create the proper exception. Peer-to-peer applications may also require port forwarding rules on the router, which is a separate step.

prompt: Windows Update repeatedly fails with error 0x80070002. The built-in troubleshooter does not fix it. What manual steps should a technician try?

options.text: Reinstall Windows — update errors cannot be fixed manually
Stop the wuauserv, bits, and cryptSvc services, rename the SoftwareDistribution folder, restart the services, then retry updates
Disable antivirus and Windows Firewall permanently to allow updates
Download updates manually from the Microsoft Update Catalog only

explanation: The Windows Update reset procedure clears the corrupted download cache: 1) Stop services: net stop wuauserv; net stop cryptSvc; net stop bits; net stop msiserver. 2) Rename the cache folders (Windows recreates them fresh): ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old and ren C:\Windows\System32\catroot2 catroot2.old. 3) Restart services: net start wuauserv; net start cryptSvc; net start bits; net start msiserver. 4) Retry Windows Update. If this does not resolve the issue, run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth followed by sfc /scannow to repair component store corruption that may be preventing updates from applying. The Microsoft Update Catalog (catalog.update.microsoft.com) allows manual download and installation of specific update packages as a fallback.

prompt: A domain user logs in and sees: 'We can't sign you in with this account — You've been signed in with a temporary profile.' Their desktop looks wrong and nothing saves between sessions. What happened and how is it fixed?

options.text: The user's password expired — reset it and log in again
The user's Windows profile is corrupted — log in as admin, delete the corrupt profile, and let Windows create a fresh one on next login
The domain controller is offline — this behavior is expected
The hard drive is full — free up space and restart

explanation: This error means Windows could not load the user's profile (it is corrupted or locked) and created a temporary TEMP profile instead. Everything the user does in a TEMP profile is lost at logoff because the TEMP profile is discarded. To fix: 1) Log in to the machine as a different local or domain administrator account (NOT the affected user). 2) Navigate to C:\Users\ and rename or delete the corrupted profile folder. 3) Open Registry Editor → HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList and delete or rename the registry key corresponding to the affected user's SID (sometimes marked with .bak). 4) Have the user log in again — Windows creates a fresh profile. Important: the new profile starts empty. Documents from the old corrupted profile must be manually copied from the old profile folder if they were not stored on a network share or OneDrive.

prompt: After uninstalling a program, another application shows: 'The program can't start because MSVCP140.dll is missing.' What is the cause and correct fix?

options.text: The application executable is corrupted — reinstall the affected application
A shared Visual C++ runtime library was removed during the uninstall — reinstall the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2019 Redistributable
Windows system files are corrupted — run sfc /scannow
The hard drive has bad sectors — run chkdsk

explanation: MSVCP140.dll is part of the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2019 Redistributable runtime package, a shared library that many applications depend on. When an uninstaller removes a shared DLL that other applications still need, those applications fail with 'DLL is missing' errors. The fix is to download and reinstall the appropriate Visual C++ Redistributable from Microsoft's website. Both the x86 (32-bit) and x64 (64-bit) versions may be needed. Common DLL errors by runtime: MSVCP140.dll / VCRUNTIME140.dll — Visual C++ 2015-2019 Redistributable. MSVCP120.dll — Visual C++ 2013 Redistributable. MSVCR100.dll — Visual C++ 2010 Redistributable. .NET-related DLL errors require installing the correct .NET Framework or .NET version from Microsoft.

prompt: A legacy business application designed for Windows XP shows display errors and instability on Windows 11. Without replacing the software, what Windows feature may help?

options.text: Run Windows XP in Hyper-V as a full virtual machine
Right-click the application → Properties → Compatibility tab → Run in compatibility mode for Windows XP
Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) can run Windows XP apps
Safe Mode runs legacy apps in a more compatible environment

explanation: Compatibility Mode instructs Windows to emulate behaviors of an older Windows version for a specific application. Options include Windows 95, 98, XP SP2, XP SP3, Vista, 7, and 8. Additional compatibility settings on the same tab include: Run as administrator (many older apps require elevated rights), Disable fullscreen optimizations (helps fullscreen apps), Override high DPI scaling behavior (fixes blurry or oversized display on high-resolution screens), and Run in 640×480 screen resolution (for very old games). Right-clicking and selecting Troubleshoot compatibility launches an automated wizard that tests settings. Limitation: 16-bit applications designed for Windows 3.x or earlier cannot run on 64-bit Windows regardless of compatibility mode — a 32-bit Windows virtual machine is required in those cases.

prompt: A user's workstation clock is 10 minutes ahead of the domain controller. The user cannot log in and receives a Kerberos authentication error. What is the cause and fix?

options.text: The user's password has expired — reset it
Kerberos requires clocks within 5 minutes of each other — correct the workstation clock and ensure Windows Time Service is running
The domain controller is offline — restart it
The user account is locked out after failed attempts

explanation: Kerberos authentication requires all clocks in the domain to be within 5 minutes of each other. Kerberos tickets contain timestamps; if clock skew exceeds 5 minutes, tickets appear expired and authentication is rejected with an error like 'Kerberos pre-authentication failed.' Fix: correct the workstation clock immediately. Domain-joined Windows machines should sync automatically from the domain controller via the Windows Time Service (W32Time). Force a manual time sync: w32tm /resync in an elevated Command Prompt. Check the time service status: w32tm /query /status. Net time sync: net time \\DomainControllerName /set /y. Ensure the Windows Time Service (W32Time) is set to Automatic start and is running via services.msc. Time drift is common on virtual machines and laptops that hibernate frequently.

prompt: A laptop is being donated to a charity. The owner wants to remove all personal data and hand the device to the new user with a clean Windows installation. Which option in Windows accomplishes this completely?

options.text: System Restore — reverts to the last restore point
Reset this PC → Remove everything → Clean the drive — removes all files, apps, and settings and reinstalls Windows
Manually uninstall all apps and delete the Users folder
Run Disk Cleanup and Storage Sense

explanation: Reset this PC with Remove everything performs a full reinstall of Windows and erases all personal files, applications, and settings. The additional option 'Clean the drive' (available during the reset process) overwrites the drive's data, making recovery of personal files significantly harder with standard tools. This combination is the appropriate choice when transferring a device to a new owner. Keep my files is a different option that reinstalls Windows but preserves personal documents — it is not appropriate for donation since personal data remains. For highly sensitive data, a dedicated data erasure tool such as DBAN (for HDDs) or the manufacturer's secure erase tool (for SSDs) provides a more thorough wipe before donation, especially when regulatory compliance is required.

prompt: A hospital data center needs a UPS solution that completely eliminates power quality issues, including momentary sags, surges, harmonics, and brief outages, with absolutely no transfer time. Which UPS type meets this requirement?

options.text: Standby (offline) UPS — switches to battery only when power fails
Line-interactive UPS — uses AVR to regulate voltage without switching to battery
Online double-conversion UPS — continuously runs equipment from battery power while the battery is maintained by the AC supply
Ferroresonant UPS — uses a transformer for regulation

explanation: An online double-conversion UPS permanently converts incoming AC power to DC, charges the battery, and then inverts DC back to clean AC to power the connected equipment. The equipment always runs from the inverter output and is completely isolated from the raw utility supply. This means zero transfer time during an outage (the inverter is already running) and elimination of all power quality issues. Standby UPS: passes utility power directly; switches to battery in 5–10 ms on failure — acceptable for most desktop equipment but not for the most sensitive systems. Line-interactive UPS: adds an autotransformer that handles voltage fluctuations without a battery switchover, with a transfer time of about 4 ms — suitable for most servers. Online double-conversion is the most expensive option and generates more heat but provides maximum protection. It is the standard for critical medical, financial, and data center applications.

prompt: A small electrical fire starts in a network switch cabinet in a server room. Which portable fire extinguisher type is safe to use on energized electrical equipment?

options.text: Class A — water extinguisher for ordinary combustibles
Class B — foam extinguisher for flammable liquids
Class C — CO2 or dry chemical extinguisher rated for electrical fires (non-conductive agent)
Class D — dry powder for combustible metals

explanation: Fire extinguisher classes: Class A covers ordinary combustibles (wood, paper, cloth) — water or foam agents are used but would cause electrocution and equipment damage if applied to live electrical equipment. Class B covers flammable liquids and gases — gasoline, oil. Class C covers energized electrical equipment and requires a non-conductive extinguishing agent: CO2 (carbon dioxide) is the most common for IT environments because it leaves no residue and does not damage electronics. Dry chemical (ABC) extinguishers work on Class C fires but leave corrosive powder that damages electronics. Clean agent extinguishers (Halon replacements: FM-200, Novec 1230) are used in fixed suppression systems for server rooms — no residue, safe for equipment. Class D covers combustible metals. Class K covers kitchen cooking oils. Always evacuate the area and call emergency services first.

prompt: A technician needs to move a 40-pound server from the floor to a rack shelf. What is the correct technique to prevent injury?

options.text: Bend at the waist and use back muscles to lift quickly
Bend at the knees with back straight, grip firmly, keep the load close to the body, and lift with leg muscles
Twist the torso while lifting to maneuver the server into position
Drag the server across the floor to avoid lifting

explanation: Safe lifting technique: stand close to the load with feet shoulder-width apart for a stable base. Bend at the knees — not the waist — to protect the lumbar spine. Keep the back straight and in a neutral position. Get a firm, balanced grip on the equipment. Lift slowly and smoothly using the large leg muscles rather than the back. Keep the load close to the body — holding it at arm's length multiplies the effective load on the spine. Do not twist the torso while carrying — turn the entire body including the feet to change direction. Lower the equipment using the same reverse technique. For servers over 50 pounds, use a mechanical lift or get a second person to assist. Remove heavy components such as power supplies, hard drives, and expansion cards before moving the chassis if the total weight is excessive.

prompt: A technician spills a printer cleaning solvent and needs to know if it is flammable and what first aid steps to take. Where should they look first?

options.text: The manufacturer's social media page
The SDS (Safety Data Sheet) for the chemical, which must be readily accessible in the workplace
The IT helpdesk ticketing system
A general internet search for the chemical name

explanation: An SDS (Safety Data Sheet), formerly called an MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet), is a standardized document that must accompany hazardous chemicals and must be physically accessible to workers at the location where the chemical is used. The GHS-standardized SDS contains 16 sections covering: identification (product name, supplier), hazard identification (flammability, toxicity), first-aid measures, firefighting measures, accidental release and cleanup procedures, handling and storage requirements, exposure controls and required PPE, physical and chemical properties (flash point, boiling point), and regulatory information. OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard requires SDS accessibility, proper chemical labeling, and employee training. In IT environments, toner, cleaning solvents, battery acid, and compressed-air dusters require SDSs. Knowing where SDSs are stored before an incident is essential.

prompt: A financial firm introduces a clean desk policy. Which security threat does this policy primarily address?

options.text: Phishing emails targeting employees
Unauthorized access to sensitive documents left unattended on desks and unlocked workstations
Ransomware encrypting shared network drives
Shadow IT and unauthorized cloud storage use

explanation: A clean desk policy requires employees to remove all sensitive materials from their workspace when stepping away: documents containing customer data, contracts, financial records, or passwords must be locked in a drawer or filing cabinet. Workstations must be locked (Win+L) even during brief absences. Sensitive documents no longer needed must be shredded using a cross-cut shredder rather than discarded in regular waste. Removable media must not be left unattended. This policy mitigates shoulder surfing (viewing sensitive content from nearby), physical document theft, and unauthorized access to unlocked computers. Clean desk policies are required by compliance frameworks including PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and SOX. Complementary controls include privacy screens, visitor escort policies, and shredding procedures.

prompt: An IT department needs to track all hardware assets including serial numbers, purchase dates, warranty status, and current user assignments. What process and tool category is used?

options.text: Change management and Change Advisory Board (CAB)
IT Asset Management (ITAM) using an asset inventory system or CMDB
Vulnerability scanning
Help desk ticketing system

explanation: IT Asset Management (ITAM) tracks the full lifecycle of hardware and software assets from procurement through retirement. Key data points for hardware assets include: asset tag number (physical label), serial number, make and model, specifications, purchase date and cost, vendor and purchase order, warranty expiration date, assigned user and physical location, current status (deployed, spare, repair, retired), and maintenance history. Common ITAM tools include ServiceNow, Snipe-IT (open source), Lansweeper, and Ivanti. A CMDB (Configuration Management Database) extends asset tracking to include relationships between configuration items, supporting ITIL-based service management. Network discovery tools (Nmap, Lansweeper agents, Microsoft Intune) can auto-populate the asset database by scanning the network. Physical asset tagging with barcodes or RFID enables scanning for physical audits. Accurate asset inventory is essential for software license compliance, budget planning, insurance, and security patch coverage.

prompt: A company is retiring 200 CRT monitors. What is the correct disposal method and why?

options.text: Place them in regular trash bins — they are old electronics with no hazardous materials
Use an R2- or e-Stewards-certified e-waste recycler because CRT monitors contain lead, cadmium, and other hazardous materials
Smash and mix with general waste to reduce bulk
Donate all to any charity regardless of condition or region

explanation: CRT monitors contain significant amounts of lead (3 to 8 pounds per unit in the glass funnel and faceplate), along with cadmium, barium, and phosphor compounds. These are classified as hazardous electronic waste and are illegal to dispose of in regular trash in most US states and many countries. Correct disposal options: certified e-waste recyclers holding R2 (Responsible Recycling) or e-Stewards certification, which ensure materials are processed safely and not shipped illegally overseas; municipal hazardous waste collection events; manufacturer take-back programs. Other common e-waste hazards include lithium and lead-acid batteries, fluorescent lamps containing mercury, and circuit boards with lead solder. Always obtain a certificate of recycling from the disposal vendor for compliance and audit documentation. WEEE (Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Directive) governs e-waste in the European Union.

prompt: An employee is terminated after running personal cryptocurrency mining software on a company workstation during business hours. Which policy did they violate?

options.text: Change management policy
Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) — which defines permitted and prohibited uses of company IT resources
Data retention policy
Software licensing agreement

explanation: An Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) is a written agreement that defines what employees may and may not do with company-owned IT resources including computers, network access, email, and storage. Typical prohibited uses include installing unauthorized software, running personal businesses, cryptocurrency mining, accessing illegal content, gaming excessively, and sharing confidential data externally. AUPs also contain a monitoring notice informing employees that the company may monitor all activity on company systems and that employees have no expectation of privacy. Employees are required to acknowledge and sign the AUP, creating legal accountability for violations. Related policies include the BYOD policy (rules for personal devices accessing corporate resources), the social media policy, and the remote work policy. Violations of the AUP may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

prompt: A company's policy requires all client email to be retained for 7 years. A technician deletes a 3-year-old email archive to free up storage space. What has been violated?

options.text: Clean desk policy
Data retention policy — which mandates minimum retention periods for different categories of data
Acceptable use policy
Change management policy

explanation: A data retention policy defines what categories of data must be kept, for how long (retention period), where it must be stored, how it must be protected, and how it must be disposed of after the retention period expires. Regulatory drivers vary by industry: legal and professional services firms typically retain client communications for 5 to 7 or more years. HIPAA requires medical records to be retained for 6 years from creation or last use. SEC Rule 17a-4 mandates financial records for 3 to 7 years depending on type. Early deletion of records subject to a retention policy may constitute evidence spoliation, which can result in serious legal penalties in litigation. Legal hold (litigation hold): when litigation is anticipated, all potentially relevant data must be preserved indefinitely, overriding normal retention schedules. Retaining data beyond the required period also creates risk — more data to protect, higher storage costs, and possible conflicts with GDPR right-to-erasure requirements.

prompt: A home office worker's PC loses all unsaved work whenever the power blinks or goes out. They currently use a surge protector. What should be added and why?

options.text: A second surge protector for additional protection
A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) because a surge protector provides no battery backup and the PC loses power immediately during an outage
A more expensive surge protector with higher joule rating
A generator that starts automatically during outages

explanation: A surge protector absorbs voltage spikes and surges that could damage equipment, but when power completely fails, the connected devices lose power immediately. It provides zero protection against data loss from outages or even brief power blips. A UPS contains a battery that seamlessly takes over when utility power fails, with no interruption to connected equipment. This gives users enough time (typically 5 to 30 minutes depending on load and battery size) to save their work and shut down gracefully, or to ride out short outages. UPS units also include surge protection. The APC Back-UPS and CyberPower series are common home and small office choices. For home office use, a basic standby UPS costing $60 to $150 provides adequate protection for a desktop computer. Laser printers should not be connected to a UPS because their fuser elements draw very high current on startup, which rapidly depletes the battery — use a separate surge protector for printers.

prompt: Which backup configuration correctly implements the 3-2-1 backup rule?

options.text: Three backup copies stored on three USB drives kept in the same office
Two daily backups to the same NAS device in the server room
Three copies of data on two different media types with one copy stored offsite or in the cloud
One production copy and one local backup with no offsite copy

explanation: The 3-2-1 rule specifies: 3 total copies of data (1 primary production copy plus 2 backup copies). 2 different media types to guard against media-specific failures (for example: internal server drive plus a NAS plus cloud storage, or on-premises disk plus tape). 1 copy stored offsite or in the cloud to survive physical disasters such as fire, flood, theft, or ransomware that encrypts all locally reachable storage. An extended variant called 3-2-1-1-0 adds: one offline (air-gapped) copy that ransomware cannot reach even if the network is fully compromised, and zero errors verified by regular restore testing. The offsite or offline copy is the most critical element — all locally reachable backups can be encrypted by ransomware if they are accessible from the infected network. Untested backups should be assumed unreliable until a successful restore has been confirmed.

prompt: A company performs a full backup every Sunday and differential backups Monday through Saturday. If Wednesday's data needs to be restored, which backup sets are required?

options.text: Sunday full + Monday + Tuesday + Wednesday incrementals
Sunday full backup and Wednesday's differential only
Wednesday's differential backup only
Sunday's full backup only

explanation: A differential backup contains all changes made since the last full backup. Monday's differential holds Monday's changes. Tuesday's differential holds Monday's and Tuesday's changes. Wednesday's differential holds all changes from Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday combined. To restore Wednesday: only the Sunday full backup and the Wednesday differential are needed, because Wednesday's differential already contains the complete set of changes since Sunday. This is a key advantage over incremental backups, which require the full backup plus every incremental in sequence (Sunday + Monday + Tuesday + Wednesday — four sets). The trade-off is that differential backups grow progressively larger throughout the week and take longer to create than incrementals, while incrementals are smaller and faster to create but slower and more complex to restore.

prompt: A user reports their email stopped working this morning. What information is most important to capture when opening a help desk ticket?

options.text: The user's favorite color and desk number
Symptoms, when the issue started, what has already been tried, affected device and user information, error messages, and priority level
Only the user's name — details can be added later
IT manager approval before any ticket is opened

explanation: Effective ticket documentation at creation captures: the user's name, department, location, and contact information; the affected computer name, model, and OS; exact symptoms as described by the user; when the issue started and whether any recent changes occurred; steps the user has already tried; exact wording of any error messages; priority or severity level based on business impact. Thorough initial capture avoids multiple follow-up calls, allows a different technician to pick up the ticket without restarting from scratch, and enables trend analysis when multiple similar tickets reveal a systemic problem. SLA compliance requires accurate timestamps. Ticketing lifecycle typically moves through: New → Assigned → In Progress → Pending (awaiting user or vendor response) → Resolved → Closed. Good ticket documentation contributes directly to the knowledge base and improves future resolution times.

prompt: A frustrated user calls the help desk saying their computer has been broken for a week. What is the best way for the technician to respond?

options.text: Tell the user to calm down before assistance can be provided

Acknowledge the frustration, apologize for the experience, and immediately focus on solving the problem: 'I'm sorry you've been dealing with this — let's fix it right now. Can you tell me what's happening?'
Transfer the call to a supervisor since the user is upset
Terminate the call and require the user to submit a written ticket

explanation: Effective help desk communication with a frustrated user: do not tell users to calm down — this typically escalates the situation. Acknowledge the user's frustration empathetically without admitting fault: 'I can hear how frustrated you are, and I want to help you get this resolved.' Apologize for the experience rather than for something specific that may not have been your team's fault. Use active listening: do not interrupt, reflect back what the user says to confirm understanding, avoid technical jargon. Transition quickly to solving the problem so the user feels progress is being made. Set realistic expectations about resolution time and follow through on commitments. Escalate to a supervisor when: the user is genuinely abusive or threatening (not just frustrated), the issue is beyond the technician's technical expertise, or a VIP is involved with urgent business impact. Clear, empathetic, jargon-free communication is a core competency tested on the 220-1202 exam.

prompt: A small business owner has just set up a new router. What are the most important initial security steps?

options.text: Enable UPnP for easy device connectivity and leave other settings at defaults
Change default admin credentials, disable remote management, enable WPA3 encryption, disable WPS, and update firmware
Broadcast the company name as the SSID for easy identification
Disable the built-in firewall for better performance

explanation: Essential initial SOHO router security steps in priority order: Change default admin credentials (username and password) — defaults are publicly documented and universally known by attackers. Enable WPA3-Personal (or WPA2-AES if WPA3 is unavailable) with a strong, random passphrase of 20 or more characters. Disable remote management to prevent external access to the admin interface. Disable WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) which has known vulnerabilities (Pixie Dust attack). Update router firmware to patch security vulnerabilities. Enable the built-in firewall (typically on by default — verify). Create a separate guest network to isolate visitor devices from internal systems. Disable UPnP, which allows devices to automatically open ports and is a security risk. Use a non-identifying SSID that does not reveal the company name or router model. Review connected devices periodically for unauthorized access.

prompt: An employee reports their company-issued smartphone stolen at an airport. What immediate action should IT perform to protect corporate data?

options.text: Call the employee and ask them to change their email password on a different device
Initiate a remote wipe through the MDM platform to erase all data on the stolen device
Suspend only the cellular account — this prevents calls but does not protect device data
Wait 48 hours before taking action in case the phone is recovered

explanation: A remote wipe via MDM immediately erases all data on the stolen device, rendering it factory clean if it connects to the network. This removes corporate email, contacts, calendar, apps, cached credentials, and any sensitive documents on the device. Steps to take immediately: initiate remote wipe from the MDM console (Microsoft Intune, Jamf, or similar). Change the employee's domain or Microsoft 365 password to prevent use of any credentials the thief may have observed. Revoke active sessions and app tokens via the identity management platform. Report the incident to the IT security team for documentation. File a police report if appropriate for insurance purposes. For BYOD devices, a selective (corporate) wipe is more appropriate as it removes only corporate data while preserving personal content. Carrier account suspension stops cellular calls and data over the cellular network but does not prevent a thief from accessing data on the device via Wi-Fi or simply reading what is stored locally.

prompt: A company policy requires unique, complex passwords for every system, but employees struggle to remember dozens of different credentials. Which security-aligned solution addresses both requirements?

options.text: Use one strong, complex password everywhere for simplicity and memorability
A corporate password manager that generates and stores unique complex passwords for every account
Write passwords in a physical notebook kept in a locked desk
Use the browser's built-in password saving feature for all corporate systems

explanation: Password managers solve the conflict between security (unique, complex passwords for every account) and usability (humans cannot memorize dozens of random passwords). Enterprise password managers such as 1Password Teams, LastPass Business, and Bitwarden for Business offer centralized admin control, shared credential vaults for team accounts, integration with Active Directory or Azure AD for SSO, MFA enforcement on vault access, breach monitoring, and audit reporting on password age and reuse. Users authenticate to the vault with a single strong master password or biometric and the password manager auto-fills credentials for every other system. Writing passwords in a notebook leaves them physically vulnerable to theft or unauthorized viewing. Browser-saved passwords lack admin control, central management, and sharing capabilities, and tie credentials to a specific browser. Reusing the same password across systems is the primary enabler of credential-stuffing attacks.

prompt: A technician needs to quickly identify the IP addresses, VLAN assignments, and switch port locations for devices in a building. Which documentation artifact provides this?

options.text: Physical network diagram (shows cable runs and equipment locations)
IP address management (IPAM) records and port assignment documentation
Logical network diagram (shows routing domains and VLAN topology)
Change management log

explanation: Different network documentation types serve different purposes. An IPAM (IP Address Management) record or spreadsheet contains: all assigned and available IP addresses, associated hostnames and device names, VLAN assignments, MAC addresses, device purpose, and physical location. A port assignment document (patch panel map) records: which switch port maps to which wall port and which device, the switch name and port number, and the VLAN configured on each port. A physical network diagram shows where equipment is physically located (server room, closets, floor plans) and how cables run between them, but does not show IP addressing or VLAN details. A logical network diagram shows how the network is structured logically (VLANs, IP subnets, routing), but not physical cable paths. Complete network documentation requires all of these working together. Well-maintained documentation dramatically reduces troubleshooting time, especially after staff turnover.

prompt: An IT department wants any technician — regardless of experience — to be able to perform a workstation imaging and deployment consistently. What document type should be created?

options.text: RFP (Request for Proposal) for imaging software
SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) documenting each step of the process in sequence
NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement) for imaging tool vendors
SLA (Service Level Agreement) for the imaging team

explanation: A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) provides step-by-step instructions for completing a specific repeatable task consistently. SOPs ensure that every technician, whether experienced or newly hired, follows the same process and achieves the same result. A well-structured SOP includes: title and purpose, prerequisites and required tools, step-by-step instructions with screenshots where helpful, decision trees for handling variations, verification steps to confirm success, troubleshooting guidance for common failures, the document owner, version number, and last review date. SOPs enable knowledge transfer when key staff leave, support compliance audits, reduce errors, and facilitate training. Related documentation types include runbooks (operational procedures for ongoing tasks), work instructions (detailed sub-steps), and knowledge base articles (issue-specific solutions). SOPs should be version-controlled, reviewed at least annually, and stored in a location accessible to all relevant staff.
